messages:
alya: heads up — onboarding an HF Llama variant and the generation_config.json import is producing output that ignores repetition_penalty in Redwood runtime :confused:
sam: can you paste the raw generation_config.json you got from HF? maybe keys got renamed or strings coerced
alya: sure — snippet:
```json
{
  \"temperature\": \"0.8\",
  \"top_p\": 0.95,
  \"top_k\": null,
  \"repetition_penalty\": 1.05,
  \"do_sample\": true
}
```
sam: hmm temperature is a string — we coerce numeric strings but fallback path might be skipping rep_penalty when top_k is null
matt: FYI we have a legacy mapping that treats top_k=null as "disable top_k" and sets an internal sampler to beam-ish fallback. That code path ignores rep_penalty in the sampler implementation. Bug.
kai: also saw quantized int8 runs where sampling mass shifts and rep_penalty effects are amplified. i ran 500 prompts with and without quantized kernels; repeat rate jumped ~7% even when rep_penalty applied.
alya: exact symptom: HF locally (float32) with same config -> reasonable diversity; on RW import + int8 -> lots of short repeated phrases. Example output: "... and then then then" vs HF: "... and then" 
jordana: can you attach a minimal repro? we should add an eval that checks ngram-repeat increase and sample entropy.
alya: minimal repro attached in thread gist: https://gist.fake/repro-gen-1977654321 — includes prompts + decoded outputs, quant settings
sam: quick workaround: set top_k to a high integer (e.g., 1000) instead of null — that forces the sampling codepath that respects rep_penalty. Not ideal but useful for testing :thumbsup:
matt: long-term fix: unify sampler selection. Conversion should map HF generation_config nulls to explicit sampler configs and ensure rep_penalty applied for all sampling backends. I'll file a small patch.
infra-bot: deploy queued for branch fix/sampler-unify — CI will run regression evals against onboarding suite
jordana: also let's add a unit test in eng-ml that imports HF generation_config.json with string numeric fields and ensures (1) temperature parsed as float, (2) top_k/top_p semantics preserved, (3) repetition_penalty honored, and (4) quantized kernels produce bounded repeat delta < 2% on our eval prompts. I'll write the test.
kai: one more data point — the tokenizer had missing <|bos|> mapping so chat templates got an extra token in front which changed context length and triggered a different batching kernel. That also changed decoding marginally; worth auditing special token mapping during import.
alya: great catch. i'll add tokenizer mapping checks to the repro. thanks everyone :pray:
